references.text: Terah took Abram and Lot with him from Ur to Haran, where Terah died. This provides the direct background for Abram's departure from Haran and explains why Lot was with him.
God reminds Abram that He brought him out of Ur in Chaldea, confirming God's guidance behind Abram's obedient departure from his homeland.
The book of Hebrews highlights Abraham's faith and obedience: when he was called, he went out without knowing where he was going, which is a direct comment on his obedient response to God's call.
Stephen refers directly to Abraham's departure from Haran after his father's death, confirming the chronology and obedience described here.
The psalmist points to God's covenant with Abraham and the promise of the land of Canaan, which was the destination of the journey Abram began when he left Haran.
